pages.text: An $(thing)Alloy$() mixes metals into a new, stronger one. Copper makes tools, but the next step up is one of three $(thing)Bronzes$(). An alloy is made of component $(thing)metals$(), each of which must stay within its share of the whole.

Early on, alloys are made in a $(thing)Small Vessel$(), much as in $(l:getting_started/finding_ores#casting)Casting$(): put in enough ore pieces in the right ratio for a known alloy. Heat the vessel in a $(l:metalworking/charcoal_forge)Charcoal Forge$(), as a pit kiln (about 900 °C) cannot melt copper (1080 °C).

Take $(thing)Bronze$() (on the right): a full 1000 mB needs 880-920 mB of $(thing)Copper$() together with 80-120 mB of $(thing)Tin$().$(br2)The three bronzes follow, one to a page. All make tools, $(l:mechanics/armor)Armor$() and more, differing a little in durability, speed and damage.

Three more alloys cannot make tools: $(thing)Brass$(), $(thing)Rose Gold$() and $(thing)Sterling Silver$().$(br2)Of these, $(thing)Brass$() goes into mechanisms, including $(l:mechanics/mechanical_power)Mechanical Power$(), and for the brass blowpipe of glassworking.$(br2)$(thing)Rose Gold$() and $(thing)Sterling Silver$() go into $(l:metalworking/steel#red_steel)Red Steel$() and $(l:metalworking/steel#blue_steel)Blue Steel$().
pages.title: Utility Alloys

pages.text: $(bold)Needs:$()$(br)$(li)$(thing)Copper$(), 62 to 72 %$(li)$(thing)Zinc$(), 28 to 38 %$(br2)Real brass for mechanisms holds about a third of zinc, and melts at 930 °C.
pages.title: Brass

pages.text: Copper smelted from tetrahedrite holds arsenic and is $(thing)arsenical$(). It can stand in for copper in bronze, bismuth bronze, black bronze and brass. Mixed with pure copper it gives arsenical copper again: arsenic is not diluted away. Pure copper comes only from native copper and malachite.
pages.title: Arsenical copper
